# Design System UI — llms.txt
# Agent instruction layer. This file is served at /llms.txt on every page so
# that terminal agents and in-page bots can operate the system without a human.

## What this is
A single-page workflow builder. A bot or human designs a ComfyUI-style node
graph, executes it in an isolated backend, and a Gemma 4 12B evaluator scores
the result and decides "iterate" or "done". Every capability below is reachable
by HTTP — no page navigation, no browser required.

## Base URL
Default: http://localhost:8000

## Actions (HTTP API)
GET  /                          -> the single-page UI (HTML)
GET  /llms.txt                  -> this file
GET  /health                    -> {status, service, timestamp}
GET  /api/patterns              -> {patterns: {id: {name, description, icon}}}
POST /api/workflow/execute      -> run a workflow, returns {status, output, results, timestamp}
POST /api/workflow/evaluate     -> Gemma 4 12B scoring, returns {score, feedback, suggestions, verdict}
POST /api/workflow/suggest-params -> {model, temperature, ...} for a node type

## Workflow object (request body for /api/workflow/execute)
{
  "id": "workflow-123",
  "nodes": [
    {"id": "in1",  "type": "text-input",  "x": 100, "y": 100, "params": {}},
    {"id": "llm1", "type": "llm-node",    "x": 300, "y": 100,
       "params": {"model": "gemma-4", "temperature": 0.7}},
    {"id": "out1", "type": "text-output", "x": 500, "y": 100, "params": {}}
  ],
  "edges": [
    {"from": "in1", "to": "llm1"},
    {"from": "llm1", "to": "out1"}
  ],
  "parameters": {}
}

## Node types
input:      text-input, file-input, image-input   (id must end in "input")
processing: llm-node, transform, filter
output:     text-output, file-output              (id must end in "output")

A valid workflow needs at least one input node and one output node.

## Evaluate response and the iterate loop
/api/workflow/evaluate returns:
  {"score": 0-100, "feedback": "...", "suggestions": [...],
   "verdict": "iterate" | "done", "model": "gemma:12b",
   "gemma_live": true|false}

gemma_live=true means a real Gemma model (via Ollama) wrote the critique;
false means the deterministic heuristic evaluator answered (Ollama not
running). Both modes return the same schema — agents need no special casing.

Recommended agent loop:
  1. Build or LOAD a pattern (GET /api/patterns for the catalog).
  2. POST /api/workflow/execute.
  3. POST /api/workflow/evaluate with {workflow, results}.
  4. If verdict == "iterate": apply suggestions[].action, go to step 2.
     If verdict == "done": stop and report score + feedback.

## Patterns (starting templates)
text-classifier, rag-pipeline, agent-loop, eval-loop
Fetch metadata via GET /api/patterns; load node layouts client-side or
construct the equivalent nodes/edges from the shapes documented above.

## curl examples
curl http://localhost:8000/api/patterns
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/workflow/execute \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"id":"wf1","nodes":[{"id":"in1","type":"text-input","x":0,"y":0,"params":{}},{"id":"out1","type":"text-output","x":100,"y":0,"params":{}}],"edges":[{"from":"in1","to":"out1"}]}'

## Going live with real Gemma (zero code changes)
Start Ollama with a Gemma model and the evaluator switches to live inference
automatically (falls back to the heuristic when unreachable):

  ollama pull gemma:12b && ollama serve

Environment overrides:
  OLLAMA_URL     backend URL   (default http://localhost:11434)
  GEMMA_MODEL    model name    (default gemma:12b)
  GEMMA_TIMEOUT  seconds       (default 60)

## Self-test
Run ./test.sh — boots the server on a scratch port and asserts every endpoint,
the iterate loop, and the Go + Rust clients (22 checks).
